chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:
For feces, wiping with stones suffices; and for urine, nothing suffices except water. And that which indicates the first interpretation.

key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ الْأَوَّلِ: the first interpretation; the earlier legal reading being supported
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: feces; here referring to excrement after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water; the required purifier for urine in this ruling
key_terms.الْمَسْحُ: wiping; cleaning by rubbing rather than washing
key_terms.بِالْأَحْجَارِ: with stones; a means of dry cleaning after defecation

ai.seo_question: Does wiping with stones suffice for purification after urine and feces in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling on purification after relieving oneself. It states that wiping with stones is sufficient for feces, whereas urine may only be purified with water, indicating the preferred legal interpretation in this context.
